products-management: Products Management Overview A product is something physical you stock, sell, or install: a filter, a thermostat, a length of pipe. Each one carries what it costs you, what you charge for it, and, if you want, how many you have. Add it to an estimate or an invoice and the price and the stock follow. From this section you can: Add products with cost, markup and price, a photo, and where they come from. Track stock : what's on hand, what's already promised, when to reorder. Edit one product, or bulk edit quantities across many. Archive products you no longer carry, and restore them later. Delete an archived product for good, when nothing references it. Search and filter by tag, group, vendor, manufacturer and more. Important: archiving and deleting are different. Archiving takes a product out of the pickers while keeping every record that used it. Deleting is permanent, and only possible once nothing references the product. The Products list To open it, go to Menu > Inventory > Products . The Products list. Cost and Item Price are sortable; Markup is not. Active and Archived Two tabs: Active , what you currently carry, and Archived , what you've retired. Archived products don't appear when you're building an estimate or an invoice, but they stay on everything they were already part of. Columns Column What it shows SKU The code that identifies the product. Set once when you create it and fixed from then on. Sortable. Product Its photo, name, and description. Hover the photo to see it bigger, which helps when two parts have similar names. Cost What you pay for it. Sortable. Markup % What you add on top. Item Price What the client pays. Sortable. Taxable Ticked when the product is included in tax calculations. In Use Ticked when at least one estimate, job, or invoice references it. This is what decides whether it can be deleted. Tags The labels you've given it. Groups The groups it belongs to, if any. Actions See below. Row actions Each row has an eye that opens View product details , a read-only view of everything about the product including its stock, and a three-dot menu with edit, archive or delete, and the rest. Delete is greyed out while anything references the product: "This item can't be deleted because it's linked to existing records." Archive it instead. Search and filters The search box in the card header matches names and SKUs, and Filter opens a panel to narrow by tag, group, and the product's other attributes. Reset Filter clears them. Filters, search, and the tab you're on all work together. Narrowing the catalogue down. Adding a product Click Add Product . A panel opens from the right, titled Add New Product , with everything on one screen: the essentials first, then the details. Cost, markup and item price are linked: fill in two and the third follows. The essentials Field Required Notes Product Image No A photo. Worth adding, because it's what someone recognises in a list of similar parts. SKU Yes A code unique to this product. You can't change it afterwards. If the code is already taken you'll be told when you leave the field. Name Yes What it's called on estimates and invoices, so write it the way a client should read it. Description No Size, model, what it fits: whatever stops someone ordering the wrong one. Cost Yes What you pay your supplier. Markup — Your margin, as a percentage. Item Price — What the client pays. Taxable No Include this product in tax calculations. How cost, markup and price fit together These three are linked, so you only ever fill in two: Enter a cost and a markup , and the item price is worked out as cost plus that percentage. Enter a cost and an item price , and the markup is worked out for you. Which way you work depends on how you price. If you apply a standard margin, type the markup and let the price follow. If the price is fixed, by a manufacturer or because that's what the market bears, type the price and see what margin it actually leaves you. The details Below the essentials sits everything that makes the product orderable and countable. None of it is required, but it's what turns a price list into a working inventory. Field What it's for Unit Of Measure How you count it: each, box, foot, gallon. Vendor / Vendor SKU Who you buy it from, and their code for it, so reordering doesn't mean hunting through catalogues. Manufacturer / Manufacturer Number Who makes it, and the part number. Average Delivery Time (Days) How long it takes to arrive. This is what tells you how early to reorder. Location Where it lives: a van, a shelf, a bay. Color When the same part comes in several. Group Which group it belongs to. Tags Your own labels, for filtering later. Quantity On Hand How many you have right now. Re-Order Quantity The level at which you want to be warned. Disable inventory tracking Turn counting off for this product. See below. Click Add Product to finish. Stock For anything you count, DHS tracks three numbers rather than one: Number What it means Stock Available What you can still promise. Stock Reserved for Estimates Already quoted, not yet committed. Stock Reserved for Jobs Committed to work in progress. The distinction is the point: ten filters on the shelf with eight already promised to jobs is not ten filters you can sell. Products show up as In Stock , Low stock , or Out of stock depending on where they sit against your re-order quantity. Products you don't count Not everything is worth counting: consumables, bulk fittings, anything you simply never run out of. Turn on Disable inventory tracking for those. They keep their price and work normally on estimates and invoices; they just don't carry quantities and won't warn you about stock. Editing a product Open the three-dot menu on the row and choose Edit product . Everything is editable except the SKU. Save with Apply Changes . Editing a product. The SKU is fixed once created. The edit panel also carries Archive (or Delete , for a product already archived), with a confirmation right there. Updating quantities for several products at once After a stock count or a delivery, editing products one at a time is a waste of an afternoon. Select the rows you want, and bulk edit lets you set Quantity On Hand and Re-Order Quantity for all of them together. The panel tells you what it's about to do: how many products are selected, and whether any of them can't be updated. Products with inventory tracking switched off have no quantities to set, so they're left out; if none of your selection is tracked, you're told that instead of the change silently doing nothing. Turn tracking on in each product's edit panel first. Bulk edit says how many products it will touch, and warns when some cannot be. Archiving, restoring, deleting To archive: three-dot menu > Archive > confirm. The product moves to the Archived tab and stops appearing in pickers. Everything that already used it is untouched. You can archive several at once by selecting their rows. Archiving asks first, and leaves every existing record alone. To restore: Archived tab > three-dot menu > Restore . To delete for good: Archived tab > three-dot menu > Delete > confirm. Only available when the In Use column is empty. Products added in a hurry Mid-estimate and the part isn't in your catalogue yet? The product picker has a Quick Add shortcut in it: give a SKU, a name and a price, and you're back where you were with the product created. Its row carries a marker until someone fills in the vendor, the unit and the quantities. Note that products are added this way only, from a picker while you're building something. The Quick Add panel in the top bar covers appointments, clients, jobs, estimates, crews, users, service items, properties and payments, but not products. Quick Add takes a SKU, a name, a price, and a starting quantity if you have one. The rest can wait. Where products are used Estimates : quoted parts. Quantities you quote are held as reserved, so a quote can't promise stock twice. Jobs : parts committed to work in progress. Invoices : what the client is billed for, with tax on the products marked taxable. Groups : a set of products and services you add together, instead of picking them one by one. Changing a product's price changes what future records pick up; records already written keep the price they were created with. appointments-management: Appointments Management Overview An appointment is a shorter stop: a site visit, a walkthrough, a quote call, a check-in. It's the thing you book before you know what the work will be. Once you do know, it turns into an estimate or a job without being retyped. From this section you can: Book appointments with a client, a property, a crew and a time. Send the details to the client and get them confirmed. Follow them through : en route, arrived, completed, or a no-show. Track time against the visit. Turn one into an estimate, a job, or an invoice , and see everything that came out of it. The Appointments list To open it, go to Menu > Appointments . Two tabs split the list: Active and Archived . The Appointments list. Scheduled For is the column you work from. Column What it shows Name What the appointment is for. Sortable. Client Who you're seeing. Scheduled For When. Sortable, and the column you work from. Crew Who's going. Status Where it stands. Sortable. Actions Edit, and a three-dot menu. For the same appointments laid out by time, use the Scheduler ; to see where they are, use Map . Narrow by status, crew and date. Statuses Status What it means Draft Being put together, not sent to anyone. Pending Sent to the client, waiting for them to confirm. Confirmed The client has confirmed. En Route The crew is on the way. Arrived They're there. Completed The visit happened. No Show The client wasn't there. Worth recording rather than cancelling, because a pattern of no-shows is something you want to be able to see. Canceled It's not happening. Crews move an appointment through En Route, Arrived and Completed from the mobile app, so the office can see the day unfold. Booking an appointment Click Add Appointment . You choose the client and which of their properties , what the visit is called , the crew , and the date and time . Booking a visit. The crew’s availability is respected while you pick. The crew's availability is respected while you pick, so you can't quietly book someone who's already out on a job. If the client isn't in DHS yet, Quick Add is in the picker. Appointments can also be created straight from the Scheduler by picking a slot, which is usually faster when you're booking around existing work. Appointment details Click an appointment to open it. This is the visit: when it is, who is going, the property they are going to, the services planned for it, and the hours the visit actually took. An appointment open. Start Timer sits in the header; the client and the conversation stay on the right. The capture was lost when staging started serving its offline screen; the record views cannot be taken from develop, whose data is QA junk. Re-shoot with scripts/kb-screenshots/appointment-detail.mjs and restore these two lines as soon as staging loads appointments again. --> The header has its name and status, a Start Timer action, and a three-dot menu. The sidebar keeps the client's phone and email to hand. This is the record you'll have open when you call to confirm. Two tabs: Overview : the appointment itself: the details, the property, and the services planned for the visit. Related Records : everything that came out of it. Sending it to the client Send to Client sends the appointment details out by email or text, with a preview first. The status moves to Pending until they confirm. This is what stops the "was anyone coming today?" call. What comes out of an appointment This is the part of the section that earns its keep. You went to look at the work; now you know what it is. The Related Records tab turns the visit into the next step, and then keeps the trail. The visit has to have happened first. Until the appointment is Completed , the tab says so and offers nothing to create: conversion to estimates, jobs and invoices is enabled once this appointment is completed . Mark the visit complete and the three sections grow their buttons. From an appointment you can create When An estimate The client wants a price before committing. Everything you gathered on the visit carries over. A job The work is agreed and just needs scheduling. An invoice The visit itself is what you're billing: a callout, an inspection, a diagnostic. Once created, each one is listed on the same tab, so the appointment becomes the thread you can follow from "we went and looked" to "we were paid". Each kind is created once: with an estimate already made from this visit, the button to make another is spent. Tracking time on a visit Start Timer records time against the appointment, which matters for visits you bill by the hour and for knowing what unbilled site visits actually cost you. The hours land in Timesheets like any other time. A note on products Appointments carry services , not products, because they're visits rather than installs. If parts are involved, that's a job, and the appointment is where you create it from. Editing, cancelling, archiving Everything that is not the timer lives in the three-dot menu beside it. The three-dot menu. What it offers depends on where the appointment is: an archived one shows Restore and Delete instead of Archive. Edit Appointment changes what the visit is. Moving it in time is Reschedule , and if the client had already confirmed, send it again so they know. Cancel Appointment when it is not happening, and set the status to No Show when the client was not there. The distinction is worth keeping, because one is your change and the other is theirs. Archive is how an appointment leaves the Active tab. There is no Delete on an active appointment at all: it appears only on the Archived tab, next to Restore . And even there, deleting is refused when the visit left a trail. The app names the reason: the appointment has a linked job, a linked estimate, a linked invoice, or linked timesheet entries. That is the point of archiving. The record of a visit that produced work is worth keeping. Where appointments connect Estimates, jobs and invoices : created from the appointment and listed on its Related Records tab. Clients : every client's record lists their appointments. Crews : assigned to the visit, and their availability is what the picker respects. Scheduler and Map : the same appointments by time and by place. Timesheets : time recorded against the visit. Common actions To do this Go here See your appointments Menu > Appointments See them on a calendar Menu > Scheduler Book one Add Appointment > client, property, crew, date Book around existing work Pick the slot in the Scheduler Confirm it with the client Send to Client Quote the work you just looked at Related Records > create an estimate Schedule work that's already agreed Related Records > create a job Bill for the visit itself Related Records > create an invoice See what came out of a visit The Related Records tab Record time on site Start Timer, or the mobile app Record that nobody was home Set the status to No Show Find today's visits Sort by Scheduled For
estimates-management: Estimates Management Overview An estimate is what you send a client before the work starts: what you'll do, what it costs, and how long the price holds. When they say yes, you turn it into a job in a couple of clicks, with no retyping. From this section you can: Build an estimate from your services and products, with a crew, a property, and a checklist. Send it to the client by email, by text, or both. Track where it stands : waiting for review, approved, changes requested, rejected. Renew one that expired instead of starting again. Convert it to a job once it's approved. Duplicate one as the starting point for the next. Download a PDF for a client who wants something printable. Set up a recurring estimate for work that repeats. The Estimates list To open it, go to Menu > Estimates . The Estimates list. Expiration Date is the column to watch. Columns Column What it shows Name What the estimate is called. Sortable. Client Who it's for. Date created When you started it. Sortable. Expiration Date How long the price holds. Sortable, and the column to watch, because an estimate that lapses needs renewing before a client can accept it. Crew The team the work is assigned to. Status Where the estimate stands. Sortable. Total What it adds up to. Sortable, so this is how you find your biggest open quotes. Actions Quick actions for the row. Statuses Status What it means Draft You're still working on it. Only you can see it, and everything is editable. Ready for Review Sent to the client and waiting on them. Approved They said yes. This is the one you can convert to a job. Changes Requested They want it different. Edit and send it again. Rejected They said no. Expired The validity period ran out. Edit it, then renew it to put it back in front of them. Search and filters The search box in the card header finds estimates by name and client. Status opens a panel with four of them to tick: Draft, Approved, Ready for Review and Changes Requested. So "everything still waiting on a client" is one click away. Rejected and Expired aren't in that panel; sort by the Status column to group those. Filter by status to find everything still waiting on a client. Creating an estimate Click Add Estimate . The panel has two steps. Step 1: the details Who it's for and what it covers: the client and which of their properties , a name for the estimate, the crew who'd do the work, an expiration date , and a checklist if the job has one. Step 1 is who it is for; step 2 is what you are charging. If the client isn't in DHS yet, Quick Add is right there in the picker, so you don't have to abandon the estimate to create them first. Step 2: the line items Now what you're charging for: the services and products that make up the work. Each comes in with its price already set from your catalogue, and you adjust the quantity. If you've set up groups , add one and its whole set of items comes in at once instead of picking them one at a time. From there they're ordinary lines: change a quantity, drop what isn't needed. Save, and the estimate starts as a Draft . Estimate details Click an estimate to open it. This is the quote as the client will see it: the work, the services and products it is priced from, the totals, and where it stands in its approval. An estimate open: its details, the services and products, and the bill. The header carries its name and status, and the buttons that matter for where it stands right now. A draft offers Submit estimate , an approved one offers Convert to job , an expired one offers Renew estimate . Behind More Actions : Duplicate , Download Pdf , and Delete . The Overview tab is the estimate itself: The details : title, crew, checklist, and the property, with Show Map to see where it is. Services and Products : the lines, with quantities and prices. Add, change, or remove them here. The bill : the subtotal, tax on whatever is marked taxable, and the total. Notes : internal, for your team. Chat : the conversation with the client about this estimate. Attachments : photos, plans, anything that supports the quote. The client sidebar keeps their phone and email to hand, so you can chase a quote without going to look them up. When an estimate has a recurring schedule, a Recurring Schedule tab appears alongside Overview. Sending an estimate to a client Open the estimate and click Submit estimate . Sending it out. Email, SMS, or both, with a preview of what the client receives. Choose how it goes out: Email , SMS , or both. Email gets a subject and a message; SMS gets a short one. Both come with sensible default wording, so you can send without writing anything. You can personalise the message with placeholders that get filled in for each client, so one piece of wording works for everyone. Message preview shows exactly what they'll receive, per channel, before it goes. Once sent, the estimate moves to Ready for Review and the client can approve it, reject it, or ask for changes from their portal. When a client asks for changes The estimate comes back as Changes Requested . Edit it, adjusting lines, quantities or the price, and submit it again. It returns to Ready for Review . When an estimate expires Prices don't hold forever, which is why an estimate has an expiration date. Once it passes, the estimate becomes Expired and the page tells you so, along with the date it lapsed. You don't have to start again: edit the estimate first , which is your chance to update prices that have moved since, and then renew it , and it goes back for review with a fresh validity period. Turning an approved estimate into a job This is the point of the whole thing. Once an estimate is Approved , Convert to job carries everything across: client, property, crew, services, products and checklist. Nothing is retyped and nothing is forgotten. Converting an approved estimate. Everything carries across; you pick the dates. You're asked for the start date and then the end date , with dates the crew isn't available marked so you don't book over existing work. You can also flag the job as a priority. When it's done, the estimate keeps a View Job link, so you can always get from the quote to the work that came out of it. Duplicating Quoting similar work over and over? Duplicate copies an estimate into a new draft, same lines and same prices, and you change the client and whatever else differs. Available from the row in the list and from inside the estimate. Duplicate, Download Pdf and Delete all live in the same More Actions menu. Sharing a PDF Download Pdf gives you the estimate as a document, for clients who want something to print, sign, or forward to whoever approves spending. Deleting Delete removes an estimate for good. It's on the row in the list, and in More Actions inside the estimate. There is no archive for estimates. A quote that went nowhere either stays in the list, where the status tells the story, or is deleted. If you want it out of the way without losing it, leave it and filter the list by the statuses you're working on. jobs-management: Jobs Management Overview A job is work you've committed to: a client, a property, a crew, a date, and the services and products involved. It's where an approved estimate ends up, where time gets recorded, and where the invoice comes from. From this section you can: Create jobs directly, or let them come from an approved estimate. Schedule them to a crew, with a start and end date. Follow them through : en route, arrived, started, paused, completed. Record visits , so a job that takes several trips is tracked trip by trip. Track time against the job, and against each visit. Work a checklist , when the job has one. Send the details to the client , and collect their feedback afterwards. Invoice the work without re-entering a thing. Set up recurring jobs for work that repeats. The Jobs list To open it, go to Menu > Jobs . The Jobs list. Scheduled is the column you live in. Column What it shows Name What the job is called. Sortable. Client Who it's for. Scheduled When it's booked. Sortable, and the column you live in. Crew Who's doing it. Status Where it stands. Sortable. Total What the work comes to. Actions Edit and delete. Search finds jobs by name and client, and Filter narrows by status, crew and dates. For a calendar view of the same work, use the Scheduler ; for a map of where it all is, use Map . Narrow by status, crew and dates. Statuses Status What it means Draft Being put together. Not committed to anything yet. Pending Sent to the client, waiting for them to confirm. Confirmed The client has confirmed. Scheduled Booked with a crew and a date, ready to go. En Route The crew is travelling. Arrived They're on site. Started Work is under way. Paused Temporarily stopped: waiting on a part, weather, a decision. Completed Finished. This is what makes it invoiceable. Canceled Not happening. The status beside a job's name is a control, not a label. This is where a job moves from one state to the next. Crews move a job through En Route, Arrived, Started and Paused from the mobile app as the day happens, so the office sees where things are without ringing round. Creating a job Click Add Job . Three steps. First the details : client, property, crew, services and products, and a checklist if there is one. Then the start date , then the end date . Dates the crew isn't available are marked, so you don't double-book them. Creating a job directly. Most arrive from an approved estimate instead. Most jobs don't start here, though. If the work was quoted, open the approved estimate and use Convert to job , and everything carries across. Job details Click a job to open it. Everything about that piece of work lives on one screen: what was agreed, who is doing it, the visits it takes, the hours logged against it, and what the client owes at the end. A job open: its details, services, products and bill, with the client and their conversation down the side. The header carries its name, the status (which is also the control that moves the job along), and a three-dot menu with the rest of the actions. While the job is still open it also carries Start Timer ; once the job is completed that button goes, since there is nothing left to time. The sidebar keeps the client's phone, email and billing address to hand. Under the client's details the sidebar has three tabs: Chat , Notes and Attachments . Chat itself splits in two, Client and Team , so a message to the crew about access or parking doesn't go to the client by accident. The job's conversation, kept beside the work it's about. Tabs across the top: Tab What's in it Overview The job itself: details, services, products, the bill, and the client's feedback once they've left it. Visits Every trip made for this job, with the time recorded on each. Checklist When the job has one: the steps to work through on site. Recurring Schedule When the job repeats. Invoices Invoices raised from this job. Visits Not every job is one trip. A repair that needs a part ordered is two visits; a big install might be five. Visits is where each one is recorded, so the time and the story of the job stay straight instead of blurring into a single block of hours. Expand a visit and its timesheet records appear: what kind of time, who, when, and why. Add Visit records one: the date , the user who made it, the time from and to , and a description . Time is split by what it actually was: Work Time : hands on the job. Job Prep Time : getting ready, loading, picking up materials. Office Time : paperwork and admin for this job. En Route : travel. Expand a visit to see its timesheet records, and to edit or delete it. One thing to know: a visit with a running timer can't be deleted . Stop the timer first. Tracking time Start Timer on the job records time as it happens, which is more accurate than remembering at the end of the day. Crews normally run it from the mobile app while they work; the office can also add time by hand on a visit. Either way the hours land in Timesheets , against the user and the job, which is what payroll and job profitability are built on. Checklists When a job carries a checklist, the Checklist tab holds the steps. Crews work through it on site and the job records what was done, which is useful for consistency and for proving it afterwards. The job's checklist. Crews work through it on site. Sending job details to the client Send to Client , in the job's three-dot More Actions menu, sends the job's details out by email or text, with a preview of what they'll receive before it goes. That's what moves a job to Pending , waiting on their confirmation. It stays greyed out until the job has a date to tell the client about. The three-dot menu holds everything that isn't in the header: rescheduling, completing, sending, cancelling, the PDF and delete. What it offers depends on where the job is. A completed job has no Reschedule and no Delete. Completing a job Mark the job Completed when the work is done, either from the status control beside its name or with Complete job in the More Actions menu. If the job carries a checklist, completing it is not a one-click move: the app puts the checklist in front of you first and asks you to review it. That's the point of having one. Completing a job with a checklist: review it, then complete. Once complete, the client can be asked for feedback, which shows on the job's Overview and feeds the crew ratings you see on the Crews list. Invoicing the work Open the Invoices tab and use Add Invoice from Job . The services, products and totals come straight from the job, so there's no retyping and nothing forgotten in the transfer. Invoices raised from this job. Add Invoice from Job carries the services and products across. The button needs something to bill: "Add at least one service or product before creating an invoice." A job can carry more than one invoice, which is how staged or partial billing works. Recurring jobs Work that repeats, like monthly maintenance or seasonal service, can run on a schedule instead of being created by hand each time. The Recurring Schedule tab is where the pattern lives, and it's also where you choose whether a change applies to this occurrence only or to the whole series . Worth being deliberate about, since one of those rewrites every future job. Editing and deleting What you can change depends on where the job is. A draft is fully editable; a job in progress or completed is progressively locked down, so history isn't quietly rewritten after the fact. Edit sits at the top of the job's Overview card. It opens Edit job details : the client, title, property, crew, checklist and priority. Dates are not in there: moving a job in time is Reschedule , in the More Actions menu, and services and products are changed on the job itself. Edit job details. What a job is and who it's for, not when. Delete is at the bottom of the More Actions menu, and on the row in the list as a bin. That menu also offers Cancel job , which is usually the more honest option. A job that's been invoiced or has time recorded against it is part of your records, and cancelling keeps that history where deleting throws it away. On a job that's already completed, Delete is gone from the menu altogether and Cancel is what's left. Where jobs connect Estimates : an approved estimate becomes a job with everything carried over, and keeps a link back. Appointments : a visit that turns into real work becomes a job. Invoices : raised from the job, with its services and products. Timesheets : every timer and manual entry lands there. Checklists : attached to the job and worked on site. Crews : assigned to the job; their availability is what the date pickers respect. Scheduler and Map : the same jobs by time and by place. Common actions To do this Go here See your jobs Menu > Jobs See them on a calendar Menu > Scheduler Create one Add Job > details > start date > end date Turn a quote into work Open the approved estimate > Convert to job Record a trip Open the job > Visits > Add Visit Record time as it happens Start Timer, on the job or in the mobile app See the hours on a job Visits > expand a visit > its timesheet records Tell the client what's booked Send to Client Work the checklist The Checklist tab, usually from the mobile app on site Bill the work Invoices tab > Add Invoice from Job Bill in stages Create more than one invoice from the same job Change one occurrence of a repeating job Recurring Schedule > this occurrence, not the series Find today's work Sort by Scheduled, or filter by status
invoices-management: Invoices Management Overview An invoice is the bill. It comes from the work, usually straight from a completed job, goes out to the client, and then you track it until the money arrives. From this section you can: Raise invoices , from a job or on their own. Send them to the client by email or text. See what's been read : sent, viewed, paid. Record payments , including part payments, with the method and reference. Chase what's late , by due date and balance. Download a PDF for clients who need one. The Invoices list To open it, go to Menu > Invoices . Due date and Total Balance together are the whole of credit control. Column What it shows Number The invoice number. Sortable. Client Who's being billed. Linked to The job or estimate it came from, so you can get back to the work behind the bill. Issue date When it was raised. Due date When payment is expected. Sortable, and this is how you find what's overdue. Status Where it stands. Sortable. Total Balance What's still owed. Sortable, so the largest outstanding amounts come to the top. Actions Edit and delete. Sorting by Due date and by Total Balance is the whole of credit control: the first tells you what's late, the second tells you what's worth chasing first. Filter by status to separate what is sent from what is paid. Statuses Status What it means Draft Not sent yet. Fully editable. Sent It's gone to the client. Viewed They've opened it, so "I never got it" has an answer. Payment in Progress A payment is going through the gateway. Paid Settled in full. Creating an invoice Most invoices shouldn't be typed at all. Open the completed job, go to its Invoices tab, and use Add Invoice from Job . The services, products and totals come straight across. To raise one directly, click Add Invoice on the Invoices list and fill in the client, the dates, and the lines. Raising an invoice directly. Billing a finished job is usually faster. A job can carry more than one invoice, which is how you bill in stages: a deposit up front, the balance on completion. Invoice details Click an invoice to open it. This is the bill itself: what is being charged, the tax on it, what has been paid against it, and how much is still outstanding. An invoice open. This one was raised from the job "Door Fitting" and has since been paid. Job Details holds the work billed; Payments holds the money. The header has its number and status, a Send Invoice button, and a three-dot menu holding Edit invoice , Download Pdf and Delete . Two tabs sit below. Job Details holds who it's billed to, the job it came from, and the services and products with their totals. Payments is where money received is recorded. The client sidebar keeps their contact details to hand for when you need to chase. Sending an invoice Send Invoice emails or texts it to the client, with a preview of what they'll receive first. The status moves to Sent , and to Viewed once they open it. Sending an invoice, with a preview first. Recording a payment Open the Payments tab and use Add Payment to record money received: Recording a payment. Less than the total is fine, and the balance tracks the rest. Field Notes Amount What was received. Less than the total is fine. That's a part payment, and the balance keeps tracking the rest. Payment Method Cash, Check, Credit Card, Bank Transfer, or Other. Transaction date When it was received, which isn't always today. Payment reference A cheque number, a transfer reference, whatever you'd need to match it to a bank statement later. Status Pending, Completed, Failed, Refunded, or Voided. Notes Anything worth remembering about the payment. Every payment is listed on the Payments tab and can be edited afterwards. The invoice's Balance Due updates as they come in, and once the balance reaches zero the invoice is Paid . The Payments tab. Each payment is listed, and the balance follows. That status on the list is why part payments are worth recording as they arrive rather than at the end: an invoice showing a small remaining balance is a very different conversation from one showing the full amount. Editing and deleting A draft invoice is fully editable. Once it's been sent, and especially once a payment is against it, an invoice is a financial record, so what you can change narrows. Correcting a sent invoice usually means issuing a new one rather than quietly rewriting the old. Delete is available from the row in the list and from inside the invoice, but think twice about deleting anything a client has already seen or paid. Edit invoice, Download Pdf and Delete sit behind More Actions. Sharing a PDF Download Pdf gives you the invoice as a document, for clients who file paper or need to pass it to an accounts department. Where invoices come from Jobs : the usual route. The Invoices tab on a job raises one from the work, and a job can have several. Estimates : an estimate becomes a job, and the job becomes the invoice. The Linked to column keeps the trail. Clients : a client's record lists their invoices, so you can see everything they owe in one place. Services and products : the lines, with tax applied to whatever is marked taxable. Common actions To do this Go here See your invoices Menu > Invoices Bill a finished job Open the job > Invoices > Add Invoice from Job Raise one from scratch Add Invoice Bill in stages Create more than one invoice from the same job Send it Open it > Send Invoice Check whether they've seen it The status. Viewed means they opened it Record money received Payments tab > Add Payment > amount, method, reference Record a part payment Add Payment with less than the total; the balance tracks the rest See every payment on an invoice The Payments tab Find what's overdue Sort by Due date Decide who to chase first Sort by Total Balance Get back to the work behind a bill The Linked to column Send something printable More Actions > Download Pdf
timesheets-management: Timesheets Overview A timesheet collects one person's time for a period, entry by entry, and carries it through submission and approval. Most of the entries are not typed: they arrive on their own when someone adds a visit to a job or an appointment, or starts a timer. From this section you can: See where the hours went , split into en route, job, job prep and office time. Add time by hand for anything the timers missed. Link loose entries to the right timesheet. Submit, approve and reject , with the rules about who can do which. Compare with last week , from the cards at the top. The four kinds of time Every entry is one of four types, and the type is what makes the totals mean something. Type What it covers Needs a job En Route Travelling to the work. Yes Work Time The work itself, on site. Yes Job Prep Getting ready for a job: loading, picking up parts, paperwork before the visit. Yes Office Time Everything not tied to a job. No The Timesheets list To open it, go to Menu > Timesheets . The Timesheets list. The delete on an approved row is greyed out, which is the rule made visible. Five cards sit above the list: Total Hours , Total en route hours , Total office time , Total job time and Total job prep hours . Each one carries its movement against the week before, so a number that jumps is visible without opening anything. Column What it shows User Whose time it is. On the Solo plan this column is not there, because there is only one of you. Timesheet Date The date the timesheet is filed under. Office Time Hours with no job attached. Job Time Hours on the work itself. En Route Time Hours travelling. Job Prep Hours Hours getting ready. Status Draft, Pending, Approved or Rejected. Actions Open and delete. Search sits in the card header. Beside it are three controls: a date range , which reads All Time until you narrow it, Users , and Status . The last two take more than one value at a time and both have a reset. On the Solo plan, and for crew members, the Users filter is not there, because there is only one person’s time to look at. An approved timesheet cannot be deleted. Its bin is greyed and says so when you hover it. That is deliberate: an approved timesheet is a payroll record. Filtering by status. Date range, Users and Status narrow the list together. Creating a timesheet Click Add Timesheet . It asks for three things: Date , required. User , required, and fixed from then on. You cannot move a timesheet to another person after it is created, so check it before saving. Crew members can only create their own. Description , optional, and worth filling in because it becomes the title you see at the top of the timesheet. Creating a timesheet by hand. The user cannot be changed afterwards. In practice you will create fewer of these than you think. With automatic linking on, the first entry of the week makes its own draft. Inside a timesheet Open one and the header carries the person's name and the status. If you are an admin or the owner, the status is a dropdown you can change directly; everyone else sees it as a label. Add Time sits on the right, and disappears once the timesheet is approved. A timesheet waiting on approval. Reject and Approve sit under the entries, and only appear once there is time to approve. Overview holds the description, the user, their crew and the date it was created, with Edit for the date and description. Time Entries is the timesheet itself: the entries linked to it, with a search box, a date range and an activity filter that narrows the table to one type of time. The table shows the job, the user, the date, the description, the type as a coloured tag and the duration, and totals at the bottom. Each row can be edited or deleted from its Actions. Adding time by hand Adding time by hand. The job is required for every type except office time. Add Time asks for the user, the date, the job, a From and To , and a description. Four rules are worth knowing before you start typing: The job is required for En Route, Work Time and Job Prep. For Office Time there is no job to give. The description is required . An entry without one tells nobody anything two weeks later. To has to be after From , and the duration cannot be zero. Neither time can be in the future. Unlinked entries Below the entries sits Unlinked Entries : time that exists but belongs to no timesheet yet. It appears there when someone adds a visit to a job or an appointment, or starts a timer, and nothing picked it up. Click one and the app asks: link to this timesheet, or select another? Link puts it here. Select another opens Link entry , where you either search for an existing timesheet or make a new one by giving a date and a user. Linking runs backwards too: Unlink on a linked entry sends it back to the unlinked pile, after a confirmation. Crew members only see their own unlinked entries. Admins and owners see everyone's, which is what makes this the place to tidy up the week. Automatic linking Most accounts never touch the unlinked list, because linking is automatic. The switch lives in Settings > Timesheet and works like this: When an entry is created or a timer starts, the app checks whether automatic linking applies to that person. If it does, it looks for a draft timesheet for the same week, Monday to Sunday. If there is one, the entry joins it. If there is not, a draft is created and the entry goes in. The main switch is account wide. Underneath it, each person can opt themselves out with Disable automatic linking for myself , which leaves the rest of the team on the account default. Submitting and approving A timesheet moves through four states: Draft , Pending , then Approved or Rejected . Action Who can do it When Submit Timesheet The person the timesheet belongs to While it is a Draft Change to Draft The person the timesheet belongs to While it is Pending, to pull it back and fix something Approve Timesheet An admin or owner who is not the person it belongs to While it is Pending Reject Timesheet An admin or owner who is not the person it belongs to While it is Pending Nobody approves their own timesheet. An admin looking at their own sees Submit, not Approve. These buttons only appear once the timesheet has time linked to it. An empty timesheet has nothing to submit, so the strip under the table stays out of the way. Where things are What you want to do Where See the week at a glance The cards above the Timesheets list Find one person's time The Users filter on the list Add time the timer missed Open the timesheet, Add Time Fix an entry The edit icon on its row in Time Entries Claim a loose entry Unlinked Entries, then Link Move an entry to another timesheet Unlink it, then link it where it belongs Send yours for approval Submit Timesheet, under the entries table Approve someone else's Open their Pending timesheet, Approve Timesheet Turn automatic linking on or off Settings > Timesheet
settings-configuration: Settings Overview Settings is where the account is configured: who you are, when you work, how things are numbered, how you get paid, and what the app tells you about. It is not in the main Menu. Click your avatar in the top right corner and choose Settings . Your Profile and Billing are in that same popover. The page has its own sidebar on the left, grouped so that personal preferences and account-wide configuration do not get mixed up: Group Sections Who it affects Personal Account, Profile, Notifications, Security, Privacy, Availability Mostly you, except Account and Availability, which are the company's Workspace Dashboard, Timesheet How the app behaves day to day Business Business, Accept Payments, Billing The whole account Integrations QuickBooks Online The whole account Each section saves on its own. There is no single save button for the page, so finish one section before moving to the next. Account The company's own details, in three blocks. Company Information is the name, contact name and address that identify the business. Billing Information is what appears on the paperwork, when it differs. Client Contact Information is the one to get right: the email and phone here are printed in the notification emails your clients receive, so it is how they reach you when they have a question. At least one of the two is required. Below that sits your client signup link and client code , both with a copy button. Send the link to a client and signing up through it connects them to your account automatically, with nothing for you to approve afterwards. Delete Sample Data clears the demonstration records the account was created with. It asks twice, and it cannot be undone. Do it once you have real data and the samples are only getting in the way. Profile You, rather than the company: first and last name, email, phone, time zone and language, plus your photo. Three things are worth knowing here. Changing your email starts a verification, and a banner tells you it is pending. The photo has to be an image under 4 MB. And the language you pick is yours alone, so one person can run the app in Spanish while the rest of the team stays in English. Your password is changed on this page too. Notifications A grid: the kinds of notification down the side, the channels across the top. Email , SMS , WhatsApp , Mobile and Desktop . Tick the combinations you want and save. If a channel is not available on your account it says so rather than pretending to work. SMS in particular can be switched off account-wide, and the grid shows that instead of silently dropping your messages. These are your preferences, not the company's. Everyone sets their own. Security Login security has one button, Sign out everywhere , which ends every active session. Use it when a phone goes missing. Known devices lists what has signed in as you: the device, its browser, when it was last seen and from what address. A device you recognise can be marked Trusted , and trusted ones are labelled so the unfamiliar ones stand out. Privacy One switch: Share optional product analytics . It is optional, it is off unless you turn it on, and the privacy notice is linked beside it. Availability When you can be booked. This is the schedule the rest of the app respects when it offers times. Start with the schedule type : General Schedule sets the hours for the whole company. Per Crew sets them for one crew, for when a team works different hours from everyone else. Under it, each day of the week takes one or more time slots, so a business that closes at lunch is two slots rather than one long one. Slots cannot overlap and cannot run past midnight into the next day. A crew's hours have to sit inside the general schedule. If you give a crew a slot outside it, the form says so instead of saving something the booking rules would ignore. Exceptions Exceptions are the days the schedule does not apply: holidays, shutdowns, the week everyone is away. Add one with a date range, and mark it Annual if it happens every year, which is what you want for fixed holidays. Exceptions are also summarised by month and by season, so you can see the shape of the year rather than a flat list of dates. Dashboard How much the dashboard shows and how it opens. Setting What it does Max List Length How many rows each dashboard list shows. Show Only New Narrows the lists to what you have not dealt with yet. Upcoming Jobs Window How many days ahead the upcoming jobs list looks. Dashboard Scheduler The default view for the scheduler on the dashboard. Scheduler Page The default view for the full scheduler page. The section also carries a recommended configuration. On a busy account, a shorter list and a narrower window are the difference between a dashboard that opens instantly and one you wait for. Timesheet One decision, and it saves a lot of manual work: automatic linking . With it on, a new time entry or a started timer joins the draft timesheet for that week, Monday to Sunday, and if there is no draft the app makes one. With it off, every entry has to be linked by hand. The main switch is account-wide. Underneath, each person can opt themselves out with Disable automatic linking for myself without changing anything for the rest of the team. See Timesheets for what linking actually does to an entry. Business The account-wide rules, in four blocks. Counter Settings Estimate ID Counter and Invoice Number Counter set where the numbering continues from, and the current values are shown beside them. This is what you use when you are moving from another system and want your invoice numbers to carry on rather than restart at one. Crew Settings Allow Crew To Access Any Job decides how far a crew member can see. Leave it off and Crew Restriction Active applies: they see and log time on the jobs assigned to their crews, and nothing else. Turn it on and any crew member can open and log time on any job in the account. Information Sharing Do Not Share Information controls whether your details are shared beyond your own account. Payment Disclaimer The small print at the bottom of an invoice. Keep the default text, which is shown to you in full, or write your own. This is also where Show Zelle Payment Option on Invoice lives, along with the Zelle details and the wording the client sees. Accept Payments Online card payments run through Stripe, and this section is the application and its status. You apply from here, giving your business type, company name and phone. The section then reflects where the application is: submitted, under review, needing extra verification, or approved with a link into your Stripe dashboard. If Stripe declines, the reason and a reference number are shown so support has something to work with. This matters beyond the settings page: until Stripe approves you, your clients have no way to pay online. In the client portal the Pay Now button is simply not rendered, so a client who cannot find it is looking at an account that has not been approved yet, not a broken page. Billing Your subscription: the plan, the seats and the invoices for the app itself. The section only appears when billing is enabled on the account. See Plans and Pricing for what each plan includes. QuickBooks Online Connects the account to QuickBooks Online so records do not have to be typed twice. Before connecting, the section explains what syncing does and offers Connect , which sends you to QuickBooks to authorise it. Once connected it splits into three tabs: Connection : status and connected date, the QuickBooks company and its ID, the environment, when it last synced, and the most recent activity. Disconnecting is here too. Sync Settings : what syncs and in which direction, one rule per record type. Sync Activity : the log. Every row shows the type, the direction, when it happened and how it ended: Synced , Failed , Skipped or Conflict . The tab carries a red count when there are errors waiting, and a conflict opens a panel where you choose which version wins. The record types that cross over are clients, products and services, estimates, invoices, payments and timesheets. Where things are What you want to do Where Open Settings Your avatar, top right, then Settings Change the phone clients see Account > Client Contact Information Invite clients to sign up Account > the client signup link Change your password or language Profile Stop an email you do not want Notifications Kick a lost phone out of the account Security > Sign out everywhere Set working hours and holidays Availability Make the dashboard faster Dashboard > Max List Length and Upcoming Jobs Window Stop linking time entries by hand Timesheet > automatic linking Continue your old invoice numbers Business > Counter Settings Limit what crews can see Business > Crew Settings Let clients pay online Accept Payments Change plan or seats Billing Send records to QuickBooks QuickBooks Online
checklists-management: Checklists Overview A checklist is a reusable list of steps. You build it once here, attach it to a job, and the crew works through it on site. It is how a job gets done the same way every time, whoever turns up. From this section you can: Build a checklist and its steps. Put the steps in work order , by dragging them. Demand a written note on the steps where "done" is not enough. Duplicate one , when the next checklist is almost the same. Archive and restore , so the active list stays short without losing anything. Checklists live on their own and get attached to jobs. Changing a checklist here does not change the copy already sitting on a job that has been worked. The Checklists list To open it, go to Menu > Checklists . Two tabs split the list: Active and Archived . Search sits in the card header and searches as you type. Column What it shows Date created When it was built. Sortable. Title The name, with its description underneath. Sortable. Options The row actions, which change with the tab you are on. Clicking a row opens the checklist and its steps. Creating a checklist Click Add Checklist . The panel asks for a Checklist Title , which is required, and a Description , which is not. Then the steps. Type a step and confirm it with the check on the right of the field or with Enter, and it drops into the list below. Add Item opens the field again for the next one. A checklist cannot be saved empty: until it has at least one step, the panel says so and the save button stays disabled. While you are still in the panel, each step can be edited or removed with the icons on its row. Description Required Each step carries a Description Required checkbox. Leave it off and the step is a tick: done or not done. Turn it on and the crew has to write what happened before the step counts. Use it for the steps where the answer matters later: a meter reading, a serial number, the reason a part was replaced. It is also protection, because a step marked as requiring a description cannot be removed from a job once the checklist is attached. The checklist Open a checklist and you get its name, a pencil to rename it or change its description, a badge saying Active or Archived , and Add Item . The steps sit in a table: Column What it does Handle Drag it to move the step. The new order saves by itself. Title The step as the crew will read it. Description Required The dot turns the requirement on and off in place, with no panel to open. Edit Changes the wording of the step. Delete Removes the step. Two steps cannot be deleted, and the app says why when you hover the bin: The last one standing. A checklist with no steps is not a checklist, so the final step stays. One that requires a description. Turn the requirement off first, then delete it. Order is worth a minute of your time. The crew reads the list top to bottom on a phone, so it should read like the work: what you do first, first. Duplicating The Duplicate action on a row copies the checklist with all its steps, and asks you to confirm first. It is the quick way to make the variant of a checklist you already have rather than typing it again. Archiving, restoring and deleting On the Active tab the row actions are Edit , Duplicate and Archive . Archiving asks you to confirm, then moves the checklist to the other tab. Nothing is lost, and jobs already carrying it are untouched. On the Archived tab the actions are Edit , Restore and Delete . Restore brings it back to Active. Delete is permanent, and it is the only one of the three you cannot undo. A checklist that is assigned to a job cannot be deleted at all. The bin is disabled and says so: the job would lose the steps it was worked with. Archive it instead. Putting a checklist on a job Checklists are attached to a job, not the other way round. You pick one in the first step of Add Job , or later through Edit job details on the job's Overview card. From then on it lives in the job's Checklist tab, which is where the crew works it, usually from the mobile app on site. Steps can also be added there for that job alone, which does not touch the checklist you built here. A job that carries a checklist will not complete in one click: the app puts the checklist in front of you and asks you to review it first. That is the whole point of having one. See Jobs Management for working the checklist on site and completing the job. Where things are What you want to do Where Build a checklist Menu > Checklists > Add Checklist Reorder the steps Open the checklist, drag by the handle Rename it Open the checklist, pencil beside the name Require a written note on a step The Description Required dot on the step's row Reuse one with changes Duplicate on the row, then edit the copy Get it out of the way Archive on the row Attach it to a job Add Job, first step, or Edit job details Work it on site The job's Checklist tab, usually on the mobile app
whatsapp-ai: WhatsApp AI Assistant Overview The WhatsApp AI Assistant is a conversational AI built right into WhatsApp that lets you manage your entire DHS business from your phone using simple text messages. Instead of switching between apps, you can search for clients, create appointments, send invoices, check your schedule, and much more, all from a WhatsApp chat. With the WhatsApp AI Assistant you can: Search and look up clients, jobs, estimates, invoices, crews, and more Create new records like appointments, clients, jobs, estimates, and invoices Update and manage existing records — change statuses, reschedule, edit fields Track time — clock in, clock out, and review timesheets Communicate — send messages and notifications to your team or clients Get reports — daily briefings, schedule summaries, and business reports Use utilities — check the weather, get directions, run quick calculations The assistant supports over 103 tools and works in both English and Spanish . You can type your requests in natural, everyday language — no special commands to memorize. Getting Started Linking Your WhatsApp Number Before you can use the WhatsApp AI Assistant, you need to link your WhatsApp phone number to your DHS account. Here is how: Open the DHS app on your phone or desktop. Go to Settings and select WhatsApp Integration . Enter the phone number associated with your WhatsApp account. Tap Link Number . You will receive a verification code via WhatsApp. Enter the verification code in the DHS app to confirm the link. Once verified, you can start messaging the DHS AI Assistant directly on WhatsApp. Authentication and Security Your account is protected. Only the phone number you link to your DHS account can talk to the assistant. If anyone else messages it from a different number, they won't be able to see any of your information. If you haven't used the assistant in a while, we may ask you to verify it's really you. When that happens, you'll get an email with a link — tap it, and you can pick up right where you left off. What You Can Do The WhatsApp AI Assistant gives you access to over 103 tools organized into the categories below. You do not need to memorize tool names — just describe what you need in plain language and the assistant will figure out the right action. Search and Look Up Quickly find any record in your DHS system by asking the assistant. Action What It Does Example Message Search Clients Find clients by name, phone, email, or address "Find the client named Maria Lopez" Search Jobs Look up jobs by client, status, date, or crew "Show me all open jobs for this week" Search Estimates Find estimates by client, status, or amount "Find pending estimates over $500" Search Invoices Look up invoices by client, status, or date range "Show unpaid invoices from March" Search Appointments Find appointments by client, date, or crew "What appointments do I have tomorrow?" Search Crews Look up crew members and their assignments "Who is on the North crew?" Equipment identification — Snap a picture of equipment or a product label and ask the assistant to identify it. Issue reporting — Send a photo of a problem at a job site and ask for guidance or to log it in the system. To send an image, tap the camera or upload icon in the chat interface, then select or capture your photo. Bilingual Support The AI Assistant provides full support for both English and Spanish . You do not need to change any settings — just communicate in whichever language you prefer. Automatic language detection — The assistant detects whether you are writing in English or Spanish and responds in the same language. Consistent responses — All information, confirmations, and follow-up questions are returned in your chosen language. Mixed-language support — If you switch languages mid-conversation, the assistant adapts. Spanish Examples "Muestra mis citas de hoy" — Show my appointments for today "Crea un nuevo cliente: Pedro Garcia, telefono 555-4321" — Create a new client "Marca el trabajo #1234 como completado" — Mark job #1234 as completed "Dame el reporte del dia" — Give me the daily briefing Plan Limits The number of AI Assistant messages you can send per day depends on your subscription plan. Plan Daily Message Limit Notes Free 30 messages/day Great for trying out the assistant Solo 200 messages/day Ideal for individual service providers Team 1,000 messages/day Shared across all team members Enterprise 5,000 messages/day For high-volume teams and large operations Message counts reset daily at 00:00 UTC . If you reach your daily limit, the assistant will let you know and suggest upgrading your plan. Tips & Example Conversations The AI Assistant works best when you use natural, conversational language . Here are some tips and examples to help you get the most out of it. General Tips Be specific — Include names, dates, and job numbers when possible. "Show me John Smith's invoices" is better than "Show me invoices." Use follow-ups — The assistant remembers your conversation context. After asking "Show me today's jobs," you can say "Which ones are incomplete?" without repeating yourself. Ask for help — If you are unsure what the assistant can do, just ask: "What can you help me with?" Combine requests — You can make complex requests like "Create a job for Maria Lopez at 123 Main St for next Monday at 9 AM and assign Crew A." Example Conversations Checking Your Schedule You Assistant "Show me today's schedule" Displays all appointments, jobs, and tasks scheduled for the current day "Any cancellations?" Lists any appointments or jobs that were recently cancelled Managing a Job You Assistant "What's the status of job #1234?" Shows job details including status, assigned crew, scheduled date, and notes "Mark it as completed" Updates the job status to Completed and confirms the change Creating an Estimate You Assistant "Create a new estimate for John Smith" Asks which property and services to include "Lawn mowing and hedge trimming at his Main St property" Creates the estimate with the specified services and confirms Time Tracking You Assistant "Clock me in to job #5678" Starts the time clock for the specified job and confirms "Clock me out" Stops the timer and shows total hours logged Security & Privacy Your data security is a top priority. Here is how the AI Assistant keeps your information safe: Authenticated access — The assistant can only access data if you are logged in with valid credentials. No data sharing — Your queries and data are not shared with other accounts or used to train external models. Role-based permissions — The assistant respects your user role. If you do not have permission to perform an action in the app, you cannot perform it through the assistant either. Confirmation prompts — Destructive actions (like deleting records) always require explicit confirmation before they are executed. Troubleshooting Issue Solution Assistant does not respond Check your internet connection and make sure you are logged in. Try refreshing the page or restarting the app. Image upload fails Ensure the image is under the maximum file size. Try a different image format (JPG or PNG). "Daily limit reached" message You have used all your messages for the day. Limits reset daily at 00:00 UTC, or you can upgrade your plan. Assistant misunderstands request Try rephrasing your request with more specific details such as names, dates, or record numbers.
appointment-line: DHS IVR Appointment Line IVR stands for Interactive Voice Response — a phone number that answers calls with an automated menu. Overview The DHS Appointment Line is an AI-powered phone system that allows callers to find service providers, schedule appointments, manage existing bookings, and request callbacks — all by voice or keypad input. The system is fully bilingual, supporting both English and Spanish. Phone Number: +1 (855) 244-4981 With the Appointment Line, callers can: Connect to a service provider by extension code, company name, or service type and location Schedule new appointments with available providers Check, reschedule, or cancel upcoming appointments Check a provider's available time slots Request a callback from a service provider Add or confirm a service address How to Call Step 1: Dial the Number Call +1 (855) 244-4981 from any phone. The system will greet you and offer a language selection. Step 2: Select Your Language English: Press 1 or simply wait — the system defaults to English. Spanish: Press 2 , or say "español" to continue in Spanish. If the system cannot detect your selection after three attempts, it will default to English automatically. Step 3: Connect to a Provider You can reach a service provider in several ways: Automatic recognition — If you are a returning client, the system recognizes your phone number and connects you automatically. Extension code — Enter the 5-digit code your provider gave you and press # . Say the company name — Speak the name of the business you want to reach. Press 9 — Search for a provider by service type and location. Connecting to a Service Provider Returning Clients If you have called before or have an account with a service provider on the platform, the system recognizes your phone number automatically: The system checks your caller ID against its records at the start of every call. If you have an upcoming appointment , the system will greet you and ask if you are calling about that appointment. If your number is linked to multiple providers , the system will list them so you can choose which one to reach. Your caller ID is used to pre-fill your name and account details so the AI can assist you without needing to ask for your information again. Extension Code Every service provider on the platform has a unique 5-digit extension code (a number between 10000 and 99999). To use it: When prompted, enter the 5-digit code on your keypad. Press # (pound) to submit. The system will connect you directly to that provider's appointment line. Extension codes are the fastest way to reach a specific provider. You can find your provider's code on their invoices, emails, or their website. Say the Company Name If you know the name of the company you want to reach, speak it when prompted. The system uses AI to match your spoken words to registered business names and connect you. If multiple matches are found, the system will list them and ask you to confirm. Search by Service and Location (Press 9) If you do not have a specific provider in mind, press 9 to search by the type of service you need: Describe the service: Say what you need, such as "plumbing," "house cleaning," or "HVAC repair." Say "any" to browse all available providers in your area. Location detection: The system automatically detects your approximate location from your phone number's area code. Adjust location (optional): Say a different city and state, or a zip code, to search in another area. Press 2 to change your location during a search. Browse results: Providers are listed and sorted by proximity. Press 0 to hear the next page of results. Select a provider: Press the number corresponding to the provider you want (1 through 8). Note: Service discovery results come with a disclaimer that listed providers are independent operators. Over 30 service categories are supported in both English and Spanish. What You Can Do Once connected to a service provider, the AI assistant can help you with any of the following: Action Description Schedule a new appointment Book a service visit by choosing an available date and time. The AI will walk you through selecting a service, date, and time slot based on the provider's availability. Check upcoming appointments Hear the details of your scheduled appointments, including date, time, and service type. Reschedule an appointment Change an existing appointment to a different date or time. Cancel an appointment Cancel a scheduled appointment. The system will ask you to confirm before finalizing the cancellation. Check availability Ask about available time slots before booking, so you can choose a time that works for you. Add a service address If your address is not on file, the AI can add it to your account during the call. Request a callback Ask the provider to call you back. The system will record your name and phone number for the provider. The AI conversation is handled by a voice assistant optimized for speed and clarity on phone calls. It understands natural language and does not require specific commands — just describe what you need. Keypad Commands You can use the following keypad shortcuts at any time during your call: Key Action When to Use # (pound) Submit input After entering an extension code or other numeric input 0 Start over / Next page Return to the beginning of the call, or hear the next page of search results 1 English / Select first item Language selection, or choosing the first option in a list 2 Spanish / Change location Language selection, or changing your search location during provider discovery 1–8 Select from a list Choose a provider or option from the current results 9 Search for a provider Start a service and location search to find available providers Bilingual Support The Appointment Line provides full bilingual support in English and Spanish throughout the entire call. This includes: All voice prompts are available in both languages. AI conversation understands and responds in your selected language. Service categories are recognized in both English and Spanish when searching. Appointment details and results are spoken in your chosen language. Language can be selected by voice — say "español" to switch to Spanish without pressing any keys. Voice Profiles Language Voice English JennyNeural Spanish PalomaNeural Supported Service Categories The system recognizes over 30 service categories. You can say the service name in English or Spanish when searching. Below is the full list: English Spanish Plumbing Plomer a HVAC / Heating & Cooling Calefacci n y Aire Acondicionado Electrical Electricidad Landscaping Jardiner a / Paisajismo House Cleaning Limpieza del Hogar Painting Pintura Roofing Techado Pest Control Control de Plagas Appliance Repair Reparaci n de Electrodom sticos Carpet Cleaning Limpieza de Alfombras Window Cleaning Limpieza de Ventanas Pressure Washing Lavado a Presi n Handyman Services Servicios Generales Garage Door Repair Reparaci n de Puertas de Garaje Fencing Cercas Flooring Pisos Concrete / Masonry Concreto / Alba iler a Tree Service Servicio de rboles Pool Service Servicio de Piscinas Locksmith Cerrajer a Moving Services Servicios de Mudanza Junk Removal Recolecci n de Basura Gutter Cleaning Limpieza de Canaletas Home Security Seguridad del Hogar Insulation Aislamiento Solar Panel Installation Instalaci n de Paneles Solares Septic Service Servicio S ptico Chimney Cleaning Limpieza de Chimeneas Drywall Repair Reparaci n de Paneles de Yeso Deck / Patio Construction Construcci n de Terrazas / Patios Interior Design Dise o de Interiores Welding Soldadura For Service Providers The Appointment Line is a powerful tool for service providers who want to give clients an easy way to book and manage appointments by phone, without managing inbound calls themselves. Subscription Plans Access to the Appointment Line is available on the following plans: Plan IVR Access Monthly Call Limit AI Scheduling Free Not included — — Solo Callback only 30 calls / month No — collects name and phone for callback Team Full AI scheduling 100 calls / month Yes Enterprise Full AI scheduling Unlimited Yes On the Solo plan , the system will collect the caller's name and phone number and record a callback request on your behalf, but it will not schedule or manage appointments directly. Shared Line vs. Dedicated Number Service providers can use the shared Appointment Line ( +1 855-244-4981 ) or request a dedicated phone number: Shared Line Dedicated Number How callers reach you By entering your extension code or saying your company name By dialing your number directly — no extension or search needed Custom greeting Not available Record a personalized greeting callers hear when they connect Marketing use Share your extension code on invoices, emails, and materials Print your dedicated number on business cards, flyers, and your website Availability All plans with IVR access Enterprise plan Extension Codes Every service provider receives a unique 5-digit extension code (between 10000 and 99999) for use with the shared appointment line: Give your extension code to clients so they can reach you quickly when they call +1 (855) 244-4981 . The code routes callers directly to your appointment system without any searching. Include it on invoices, estimate PDFs, emails, and marketing materials for repeat clients. Custom Greeting Management (Dedicated Numbers) If you have a dedicated phone number, you can manage your caller greeting at any time by calling your dedicated number from your registered phone: Record a new greeting — personalize what callers hear when they connect. Listen to your current greeting — hear what callers experience before they reach the menu. Reset to the default greeting — remove your custom recording and return to the system default. Greeting management is PIN-protected to ensure only authorized users can make changes. Caller Identification & Client Matching The system automatically recognizes callers who have an account linked to your business: The caller's phone number is checked against your client list at the start of each call. Recognized clients are greeted by name and connected to your appointment system without needing to identify themselves. If a caller has an upcoming appointment with your business, the system surfaces it immediately so the caller can confirm, change, or cancel it quickly. New callers are asked for their name before connecting, and this is recorded for your reference. Business Context Awareness The AI uses information from your service provider profile to provide relevant responses: Service categories you offer inform what the AI discusses and offers to book. Service area (city and state from your billing address) is used to confirm location relevance for callers. Business hours / availability from your schedule are used to suggest appropriate time slots. After-Hours Handling The Appointment Line supports customizable messaging for calls received outside your configured business hours. Callers will hear a tailored after-hours greeting and can still request a callback so no lead is missed. Emergency Transfer When a caller uses urgent language, the system can offer a direct transfer to an on-call number for immediate assistance. This ensures time-sensitive calls are never left unanswered. Tips for Callers Speak naturally. The AI understands conversational language. You do not need to use specific commands — just describe what you need. You can press keys or speak at any time. The system accepts both voice and keypad input throughout the call. Press 0 to start over. If you get lost or want to begin again, press 0 at any point. Say "any" to browse all services. When searching by service type, say "any" to see all available providers in your area regardless of category. Have your information ready. For faster service, know the date and time you prefer before calling. Call from your registered number. If you want to be recognized as a returning client, call from the phone number associated with your account. This skips the identification step and pre-loads your appointment history. Say "goodbye" to end the call. You can end the AI conversation at any time by saying "goodbye" (or "adi s" in Spanish). Coming Soon The following features are under active development and will be available in a future release: Call recording — Recordings of calls through your dedicated number will be stored securely and available for playback in your dashboard. SMS follow-ups — After a call, the system will automatically send the caller a text message confirming their appointment or callback request. Voicemail — Callers will be able to leave a voicemail when the AI is unable to assist or at the caller's request, with recordings delivered to your dashboard. Spam protection — Automatic detection and filtering of known spam callers to protect your call quota.

vendors-manufacturers-groups: Vendors, Manufacturers & Groups Overview Three short lists sit alongside your catalogue and make it easier to work with: Vendors : who you buy from. Attach one to a product and reordering stops being a search through old invoices. Manufacturers : who makes it. This is what answers a warranty call two years after the install. Groups : sets of items that always go out together, so you add the whole set in one step instead of picking parts one by one. All three live under Menu > Inventory , and all three work the same way: a list, a panel to add or edit, a read-only view, and a delete. None of them can be archived. Unlike products and services, these are either there or they aren't. Vendors Go to Menu > Inventory > Vendors . The list shows each vendor's Name , Company , Phone , Email and Address . Each row has buttons to view the vendor's details, edit them, or delete the vendor.
